headline: According to Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat, Russia has resumed using North Korean Hwasongpho-11Ga (Hwasong-11A) tactical ballistic missiles, better known as the KN-23, against Ukraine. Early battlefield wreckage analyses and tracking data from 2024 showed that the missile performed poorly. Early production batches suffered from guidance and manufacturing flaws, resulting in a reported circular error probable (CEP) of around 800–1,000 meters, and in some cases even missing targets by several kilometers. By comparison, Russia's Iskander-M has a CEP of about 5–10 meters. Following its poor performance, North Korea reportedly introduced a series of upgrades to the Hwasongpho-11Ga. These improvements are believed to have reduced the missile's CEP to around 100–200 meters, with later versions reportedly achieving a CEP of as little as 1–5 meters.

headline: The War Zone reports Boeing has taken another $280 million loss on the VC-25B Air Force One program, pushing the company's total losses above $3 billion under its fixed price contract with the U.S. Air Force. Boeing says the additional investment is intended to keep the program on track for the first aircraft delivery in 2028, roughly four years later than originally planned. The report also follows last week's announcement that the interim VC-25B "Bridge" aircraft, converted by L3Harris from a donated Qatari 747-8, will be removed from service for about a month to receive additional upgrades after concerns emerged about its defensive and mission capabilities. The War Zone has previously reported that the Bridge aircraft lacks some capabilities planned for the production VC-25Bs, while President Trump recently said its capabilities would be "maxed out." Separately, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) reported in June that the government's estimated acquisition cost has increased from $6.263 billion to $6.608 billion, underscoring the continued schedule delays, technical challenges, and rising costs surrounding the long-running replacement of the Air Force's aging VC-25A fleet. Source: https://www.twz.com/air/boeing-has-now-eaten-3b-in-air-force-one-cost-overruns
